intro: If you want a place in Uthai Thani where you open your door to a wide river and a cool breeze rather than a room in a building downtown — Uthai River Lake Resort is the riverside spot that lovers of quiet keep coming back to · It sits in the Koh Thapo area of Mueang Uthai Thani, wrapped by the Sakae Krang and Chao Phraya rivers at a point where the water spreads so wide it looks like a lake · There are air-conditioned river-view and garden-view rooms, an outdoor pool, riverside swings and hammocks, a viewing jetty, the River Lake Cafe & Restaurant, and free parking · SHA-certified, with rates from approx. ฿1,390/night

body.html: What sets Uthai River Lake Resort apart from most places in central Uthai Thani is that it genuinely sits on the river, in the Koh Thapo area where the water is wide enough to look like a lake · Most accommodation in town is a boutique or small hotel built for walking around, but this is a full riverside resort with a jetty, swings, canvas hammocks and seating that faces the water · So most guests are people who come specifically to relax quietly and watch the river, rather than to walk the markets or fill the day with activities in town.

It's in Tambon Koh Thapo, across the Sakae Krang river from the town centre · It's about a 10-minute drive into central Uthai Thani and the riverside morning market · It's near the Koh Thapo suspension bridge, the Trok Rong Ya walking street, and Wat Tha Sung (the Glass Temple), about 15 minutes away · The upside is the quiet and the full dose of nature, but the trade-off is that the entrance is fairly hard to find without GPS, and there are no shops nearby — you'll need a car every time you head out.

Rooms are air-conditioned with a balcony or sitting porch, a sofa, fridge, TV and an en-suite bathroom with a shower · There are two main types: Superior (queen or twin beds) and Deluxe, which you can take with either a river or a garden view · Real reviews praise the spacious rooms, comfortable beds and good air-conditioning, and call the river-facing rooms the clear highlight worth paying for · The thing to accept is that the resort has been open a while, so some rooms and decor feel a bit dated — this is not a brand-new property.
"A peaceful, private riverside stay — you can sit by the water all day. Helpful staff, clean rooms and a really beautiful river view. Great for a relaxed getaway."

What guests mention most is the riverside atmosphere and the lounging spots · There's a jetty reaching out over the river, swings and canvas hammocks to lie back in, and a riverbank garden you can stroll and photograph — many say late afternoon, when the light hits the water, is the loveliest time · There's an outdoor pool to swim in, and the riverside River Lake Cafe & Restaurant is open roughly 8am to 8pm, so you can sip a coffee or eat with a river view · Massage and spa are available, and there's free private parking, so it suits people arriving by car.

Let's be straight about the limits, because they're real · Reviews of the food are mixed — some praise the kitchen, while others say the Thai dishes don't quite hit the mark and that breakfast is acceptable but not varied · The Koh Thapo location, while peaceful, is remote and hard to find for anyone without a car · And a few reviewers feel the price relative to the slightly aged rooms can feel a touch high in some periods — so look at the room photos and compare rates across platforms before you book.

Overall, Uthai River Lake Resort scores around 7.6 on booking platforms and 4.1 out of 5 on TripAdvisor across dozens of guests, who mainly praise the riverside setting, the quiet, the river-view rooms and the staff · It isn't a shiny new luxury resort, but measured on actually sleeping by the river, having a pool, waterside lounging spots, a cafe with a water view and free parking — from around ฿1,390, rising with the season and room type — it lands well for anyone who wants to escape town and rest quietly by the water in Uthai Thani.

A tip from reading the reviews: choose a River View room if you want the full experience, because the water view is the main reason people come · Driving yourself is easiest — keep GPS on, as the entrance is tricky to find · Plan your main meals in town too, since there are no shops nearby and the in-resort food reviews are mixed · And try sitting by the water at dawn, when mist drifts over the river, and again in the late-afternoon light — the two times the riverbank is at its best.

honestSummary: Uthai River Lake Resort is the pick for anyone who wants to escape town and sleep quietly by the river, with lake views, a pool and waterside lounging spots on a mid-range budget — river-view rooms, a riverside cafe and free parking, from around ฿1,390 · The trade-offs are the remote, hard-to-find Koh Thapo location, mixed food reviews, and a resort that is showing its age.
honestChecks: If you want to stay downtown and walk to the market and Trok Rong Ya walking street — this is on Koh Thapo, across the river, requiring a drive into town → if you're focused on walking around town, consider a boutique in the centre instead
If you expect the resort's food to be a highlight — reviews are mixed, praised by some and criticised by others → plan your main meals in town and use the riverside cafe for coffee and snacks

If you want a brand-new, flawless room — this property has been open a while and some rooms feel dated → study the room photos, choose a river-view room, and compare rates across platforms before booking

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Uthai River Lake Resort

faq.q: Where is Uthai River Lake Resort in Uthai Thani, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Uthai River Lake Resort is at 8 Moo 5, Tambon Koh Thapo, Mueang Uthai Thani, on the Sakae Krang–Chao Phraya rivers · It's about 5 minutes from the Koh Thapo suspension bridge · about a 10-minute drive into central Uthai Thani and the riverside morning market · and around 12–15 minutes to Wat Tha Sung (the Glass Temple) and Khao Sakae Krang.

faq.q: How much does Uthai River Lake Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿1,390/night for a Superior room · Options run from Superior, Superior River View and Deluxe Garden View up to the Deluxe River View, the highlight room · All rooms are air-conditioned with a balcony, fridge and en-suite bathroom · Prices rise with the season and room type, and there are sometimes advance-booking deals — always compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Uthai River Lake Resort have river views and a pool?
faq.a: Yes to both · The resort sits on the Sakae Krang–Chao Phraya rivers in Koh Thapo, where the water spreads wide like a lake, with river-view rooms, a jetty, riverside swings and hammocks, and an outdoor pool · The riverside River Lake Cafe & Restaurant is open roughly 08:00–20:00 for coffee or a meal with a water view.

faq.q: Is Uthai River Lake Resort hard to reach? Do I need a car?
faq.a: You should drive yourself and keep GPS on · The Koh Thapo location is quiet but fairly hard to find first time, and there are no shops nearby, so you'll need a car each time you head into town to eat or sightsee · Free private parking is available.

faq.q: What is the food like at Uthai River Lake Resort?
faq.a: There's the riverside River Lake Cafe & Restaurant serving Thai food and drinks · Food reviews are mixed — some praise the kitchen, while others say the Thai dishes fall short and breakfast is acceptable but not varied · It's best to plan your main meals in town and use the cafe for coffee and snacks by the water.

faq.q: Who is Uthai River Lake Resort best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for couples and small groups who want to escape town and stay quietly by the river, with lake views, riverbank lounging and a pool on a mid-range budget · It's less suited to people without a car who want to stay downtown and walk around, or anyone expecting a brand-new resort with in-house food as a selling point.
